blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The agriculture industry in the Philippines is gaining attention as the government seeks to attract $57.4 million in investments during the Hand-in-Hand Investment Forum hosted by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO). Taking place from October 13 to 16 in Rome, the forum brings together governments, financial institutions, and private investors to explore agricultural opportunities. The Philippines is pitching proposals for five priority products: coffee, seaweed, mango, jackfruit, and cocoa. These investments aim to create jobs in rural communities, increase farmers’ incomes, and strengthen the sector’s resilience to climate change. READ: PH seeks $57.4M in […]...
